related_questions.question: What's a good FICO score for auto loan?

text_blocks.snippet: A good FICO score for an auto loan generally falls within the "Good" to "Excellent" range, typically 670 or higher. While you can get an auto loan with a lower score, a higher score usually means better interest rates and loan terms.

list.snippet: Excellent (740-850): These scores typically lead to the best interest rates and loan terms.
Good (670-739): This range still offers favorable loan options and interest rates.
Fair (580-669): You can still get a loan, but interest rates might be higher.
Poor (below 580): You may still qualify for a loan, but interest rates will likely be significantly higher, and you might need to explore bad credit auto loans.

text_blocks.snippet: Why is a good FICO score important for auto loans?

list.title: Lower interest rates:
list.snippet: A higher FICO score allows you to qualify for lower interest rates, saving you money over the life of the loan.

list.title: Better loan terms:
list.snippet: You may have more flexibility with loan terms, such as a longer loan term to lower monthly payments or a shorter term to pay off the loan faster.

list.title: Higher approval odds:
list.snippet: A good FICO score increases your chances of getting approved for an auto loan.

text_blocks.snippet: Factors that influence FICO auto scores:

list.snippet: Payment history: Making on-time payments is crucial.
Credit utilization: Keeping your credit card balances low is important.
Length of credit history: A longer credit history generally helps.
Mix of credit: Having a mix of credit accounts (like credit cards and loans) can be beneficial.
New credit: Applying for too much new credit in a short period can negatively impact your score.
